screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-agent-trust
screenshots.alt: The Codex trust switch in Settings, explained as off by default and applying only to managed checkouts, with the switch that shows Codex's hint beside its trust question.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-initial-prompt
screenshots.alt: The session launcher's initial prompt field with a prompt typed, explained as the agent's first message when the session starts.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-wrapper-prefix
screenshots.alt: The session launcher's wrapper prefix field with nice -n 10 typed, explained as running the agent while Farhelm keeps its status, conversation and Restart.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-template-sequence
screenshots.alt: The note Ctrl+Shift+X brings up, asking for template number keys and Enter, explained along with Cmd+X in the Mac app.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-template-list
screenshots.alt: The template list Ctrl+Shift+J opens, with its search box and three templates, explained along with Cmd+J on a Mac.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-quick-launch-naming
screenshots.alt: The name sessions on quick launch switch in Settings, explained as offering to name a quick-launched session.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-permission-words
screenshots.alt: The session launcher's search with perms: typed, listing yolo, guarded and custom, explained along with guarded and effort:default.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-local-host-appearance
screenshots.alt: The local host's settings with its icon and color choices, explained as working like a remote host's.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-terminal-frames
screenshots.alt: The color terminal frames by host switch in Settings, explained as off by default.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-host-steps
screenshots.alt: A host's setup confirmation listing its numbered steps and the files each writes.

screenshots.name: release-notes/v0-30-0-session-details
screenshots.alt: An open session with its tabs and buttons in one row at the top, and its name, host, directory and command in a slim bar under the terminal.
